messages.author: fee10b80f56c59e9
messages.subject: Additive effect
parts:
Hi
Is it possible to calculate the additive effect (say of the "A" allele) when I am using a backcross population developed by backcrossing a RIL F9 population to one of the parents. All my genotypes are either AA or AB.
Thanks
Savithri

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Additive effect
parts:

I'm not sure I understand. Did you just cross the RIL line to one of the parents to get the F1 hybrid, or did you do a formal backcross with the RIL and progenitor as parents, like (RIL x A) x A?

And do you have a particular QTL for which you want to determine the additive effect?

karl

messages.author: fee10b80f56c59e9
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Additive effect
parts:
Hi Karl
Sorry, I did not see your post earlier.
 
The population was created by using a RIL (9th generation). This RIL population consisted of 125 individuals. Each of these125 individuals was backcrossed to one of the parents to generate a backcross population (of 125 individuals). So I have only AA (Homozygous) and AB (Heterozygous) alleles in this population. I do not have the BB allele.
 
Yes I do have a QTL of interest that I want to calculate the additive effect. The way I mapped this population though (in WinQTL) is that I treated it as a RIL (and changed all the AB alleles to BB), since WinQTL did not have an option for the type of cross we generated.
 
And that is why I was not sure if I can use the additive effect from the output file (since the additive effect calculated would be treating my population as a RIL).
Just yesterday one of my collegues suggested teating my population as a backcross and reducing the genetic disatnce by half (to account for the RIL part of the design). 
 
This is what I got for the additiive effect for 2 QTLS when I treated it as a RIL or a BC.
Additive(H1)
BC 3.95
RIL 1.75
BC 1.30
RIL 0.66
 
Thank you
Savithri

messages.author: 96353e7106735838
messages.subject: Re: [Rqtl-disc] Additive effect
parts:
The additive effect for backcross is taken as the difference between the two genotypes.
The additive effect for RIL is taken as half the difference between the two genotypes.

So I'd take the results for RIL but divide by two because of the special form of your cross.

karl
